TR-MCP-FEDERATION-014.description: MigrationManifest binds MigrationId, mode, ProjectId, source provider/snapshot hash, schema versions, table counts, typed row hashes, alias decisions, audit backfill and immutable destination commit. Ph3 implements seed, dry-run/resume/verify and Dolt-to-new-SQLite project recovery; join is unavailable until Ph6 review/publication exist. Both lab sources are SQLite; PostgreSQL and SQL Server remain supported fixture sources. Retain originals read-only. Recovery quiesces the owner and captures every branch, including unpublished heads and dirty working sets, without creating history commits. Export one new compatible SQLite DB per branch containing ALL B2-classified versioned domains: TODO child/link/document graphs, requirements/mappings, use-case actors/flows/steps, workspace memories, portable configuration, promoted session graphs and permanent aliases. Preserve IDs, values, timestamps, versions, soft deletes and audit linkage. Manifest binds branch/head/working-set/schema/count/hash evidence; retain immutable Dolt objects/refs to preserve ancestry outside SQLite. export-todos remains a subset, never whole-project rollback acceptance. Missing domain/branch or failed validation blocks routing changes. Operator selects the verified active snapshot; others remain readable recovery artifacts. Capture host-local control/audit/outbox/IdentityServer backups at the same quiescence boundary and verify restore plus hub audit resend. Cutover requires verified receipts, explicit DEPLOY HOLD release and one-node soak before the second host.
TR-MCP-FEDERATION-014.title: original-provider-to-Dolt migration tool contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given base priority=low, A1 priority=high and B1 priority=medium, when B integrates A1, then needs_review shows low/medium/high, B/main remains B1 and no public ref is overwritten.
Given A1 deletes T1 and B1 edits T1.title, when histories merge, then needs_review retains B1 and the deleted/edited alternatives for review.

Given separate commits add T1 dependsOn T2 and T2 dependsOn T1, when Dolt merges without cell conflicts, then domain validation records dependency_cycle and leaves the prior valid live head unchanged.
Given a resolution preview binds local=B1 and incoming=A1, when incoming advances to A2, then resolve returns409 stale_review with no merge commit.

Given unresolved needs_review at12:00, when the clock reaches12:15, then plugins/status and the operator inbox show warning with ReviewId and age900s; at24h severity is critical, with at most one repeat per hour.
Given Atlas/main is blocked by review R1, when Atlas/feature publishes F2 and another project publishes X1, then both succeed while Atlas/main remains unchanged.

Given A changes title and B changes description with no domain violation, when merge runs, then both values survive; competing priority or completion edits produce needs_review instead of choosing a timestamp winner.

TR-MCP-FEDERATION-007.description: Review record key=ReviewId UUID; fields ProjectId,Branch,baseHeads[],localHead,incomingHead,candidateRef,conflictingCells[],validationErrors[],createdUtc,lastNotifiedUtc,resolution,actor. GET conflicts and status expose it. Resolve binds exact heads and returns409 stale_review if changed. Safe TODO policy: identical concurrent values collapse; edits to different cells may merge only if invariants pass; duplicate immutable child IDs deduplicate only when bytes agree. Status, priority, title, description, dependency deletions and same-cell disagreements always require review; no timestamp last-writer-wins. Notify immediately in status and durable operator inbox; warn at15min, escalate at24h, repeat at most hourly; no email/Slack sent implicitly. Same-branch dependent commits wait; unrelated branches/projects continue.
TR-MCP-FEDERATION-007.title: reviewed conflicts and valid merges contract

TR-MCP-FEDERATION-016.description:
BranchLease key=(ProjectId,Branch), OwnerSessionId, Fence int64, ExpiresUtc and WorkingSetFingerprint. Every live-branch mutation holds the same host-owner write gate across lease validation and transaction/commit. Expiry rejects new admission; an admitted write finishes before takeover. Isolated worker rights cover only non-live integration refs and it invokes owner API for live moves. Dirty takeover needs explicit review. Commit requestId persists in history for idempotency; preview binds exact head/fingerprint.

Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.
TR-MCP-FEDERATION-016.title: safe shared-host editing and commit ownership contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given keys sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt, when runtime and design-time factories resolve them, then each selects its own strategy/migration history; unknown key returns unsupported_provider.
Given empty standalone Dolt then baseline schema1, when baseline and additive schema2 apply, then CRUD succeeds, data remains intact and repeated apply makes no further changes.
Given recorded hashes of the three original migration chains, when Dolt support is added, then those hashes match and all three real-provider upgrade fixtures pass.
Given application supports schema1, when opening schema2 for domain writes, then incompatible_schema is returned before mutation.
Given a versioned project at schema1, when application starts, then no EF migration executes and its Dolt head/schema remain unchanged.
Given B1 is unpublished on schema1 and hub S1 adds schema2 from C0, when preflight/upgrade and merge succeed, then B/main=M1 with both B1 and S1 ancestors and B1 row values preserved.
Given main accepts S1 but feature still uses schema1, when feature is selected for writes, then it remains closed until its own merge with S1 validates.
Given any local branch has a draft, when Nuke preflight runs, then409 maintenance_not_ready prevents binary replacement and preserves the draft.
Given unpublished feature lacks an expand-schema attestation, when contract migration is requested, then it is refused even if all public remote branches are current.
Given a ready public main but an unattested local feature, when deployment runs, then no binary/service/schema change occurs; explicit branch attestation is required.

Given one Windows worker owns Atlas, when a second process starts or the owner crashes, then concurrent ownership is denied and restart recovers only after the OS releases its lock; committed rows and unpublished heads survive.

Given isolated disposable Atlas stores on LAB and LEGION and FED-ATLAS-H/A/B fixtures, when Ph8 partitions/reconnects each control, publication/history, audit and identity path and restarts each application/worker, Dolt, gateway, identity and control/audit component at commit/publication/report boundaries, then every matrix row records exact heads/ancestor sets/rows/drafts/refs/epoch and audit receipts matching the workflow outcome, with zero missing provider/migration/recovery rows. Missing any component/path row fails acceptance; unrelated live projects retain their provider mappings and data.

TR-MCP-FEDERATION-013.description: Provider key dolt has a dedicated migration assembly; original provider migrations remain unchanged. Versioned project schema migrations are authored only by hub maintenance on maintenance/schema-N and distributed as history. MaintenanceReadiness binds epoch, binary/schema versions, all local branches including unpublished ones, heads, working-set hashes and attestations. Preflight must pass before Nuke swaps binaries; dirty/unattested branch=409 maintenance_not_ready. LAB uses pinned Linux image; LEGION uses checksum-pinned native Windows dolt.exe under a Windows host whose actual service identity, account, ACLs and child-process start/stop/crash cleanup must be evidenced in Ph0 B1/B9; no existing suitable service is assumed, local paths on F: and exclusive Windows file handle/named mutex ownership. All B1-B12 are evidenced on both OSs.
TR-MCP-FEDERATION-013.title: Dolt fourth-provider support and schema migration contract
